page: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v6 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled with a 2835 GB local disk, and the instance supports Premium Storage. No GPU accelerators are present on this virtual machine, which runs under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the top tier for single-core CPU performance and multi-core Geekbench scores. Multi-core processing, cached memory bandwidth, and database operations score in the top 25%, demonstrating strong capabilities in parallel execution and memory-bound tasks. However, uncached large-block memory read and write speeds fall into the average range, as does static web serving throughput.

While the server performs exceptionally well on small-model LLM inference, text generation using large 70B models is a notable performance bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 10%. This makes the instance highly suitable for relational databases, software compilation, multi-threaded data processing, and general-purpose enterprise applications, but less optimal for heavy generative AI workloads. The high resource density and local storage capacity offer solid qualitative cost efficiency for data-intensive workloads.
description: The Microsoft Azure D48ads_v6 is an x86_64 general-purpose server instance powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs, 192.0 GB of system memory, and 2835 GB of bundled local storage. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance excels in CPU-heavy tasks, achieving top-tier single-core and multi-core benchmark results. Memory bandwidth for cached small blocks and database operations are highly competitive, though uncached large-block memory performance remains average. Lacking a GPU, it exhibits poor performance on large-scale LLM text generation. Consequently, this instance is best suited for database hosting, multi-threaded software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring a balanced ratio of compute, memory, and high-capacity local storage.
